title: O-INTERPRETATION-2 / P-1 amendment
status: registered before any T-E4 or T-E4K1 matrix data exists
authority: The project owner's decision on pre-treatment finding P-1, taken while the experiment was still blind to treatment: no T-E4 or T-E4K1 matrix cell had run. The statement, the four rules and the rationale are the owner's text verbatim; only code formatting is removed.
preservation: Pre-registration v1 and analysis freeze v1 are preserved permanently, byte for byte. Nothing in them is edited, and every v1 hypothesis, criterion, row and conclusion keeps its registered wording. Pre-registration v2 is pre-registration v1 together with this amendment.

finding.evidence: Control data only: C-E4 read against itself.
finding.text: A no-effect treatment satisfies both "H0" and "¬H1 ∧ H3". Control against itself, every P-PAR unit is STAYS, so E4-H0 is SUPPORTED, E4-H1 is REFUTED and E4-H3 (STAYS ≥ 2/3 of OPENING-ONLY P-PAR) is SUPPORTED. Under O-INTERPRETATION the rows "¬H1 ∧ H3" and "H0" therefore both apply.

statement: H3 is not independently mechanism-identifying because the H3 STAYS signature is also expected under the global-null condition.

rules.text: If H0 is satisfied, H0 takes precedence over ¬H1 ∧ H3. H3 is reported as consistent with opening-pass persistence but is non-discriminating under the global null.
H1 ∧ H3 ∧ ¬H2 retains its registered interpretation. The contrast between MULTI-PASS change and OPENING-ONLY persistence provides the discriminating signature.

If ¬H0 ∧ ¬H1 ∧ H3 occurs and no other registered interpretation applies, do not conclude that the residual is caused by the opening-pass effect. Report: “No registered causal interpretation applies; H3 persistence is consistent with, but does not identify, an opening-pass mechanism.”
No hypothesis definition, threshold, population, metric, contest classification, matrix cell, treatment, or analyzer calculation changes.

rationale: H3 is still useful. In the expected H1 ∧ H3 ∧ ¬H2 result, its value comes from the contrast:
MULTI-PASS units react to the mirrored order.
The privilege does not follow the new final chunk.
That remains the clean signature E4 was designed to look for. We only need to prevent H3 from being treated as affirmative causal evidence when essentially nothing changes.

reading.text: O-INTERPRETATION is applied first, unchanged, and its result is reported as the v1 reading. O-INTERPRETATION-2 then acts only when the row "¬H1 ∧ H3" applies, and reads statuses as O-INTERPRETATION does (plain: SUPPORTED; negated: REFUTED). Rule 1: when E4-H0 is SUPPORTED, the row "¬H1 ∧ H3" is withheld, "H0" stands, and E4-H3 carries the rule-1 note. Rule 3: when E4-H0 is REFUTED and none of the other main rows ("H1 ∧ H3 ∧ ¬H2", "H1 ∧ ¬H3 ∧ ¬H2", "H2", "H0") applies, the row "¬H1 ∧ H3" is withheld and the rule-3 outcome is reported in its place; the "none" row is not added beside it, because the outcome itself states that no registered causal interpretation applies. The pathology row (H5, H6, H8) is recorded whatever else holds and is not a causal interpretation, so it neither blocks rule 3 nor is removed by it. Rule 2 needs no action: the row "H1 ∧ H3 ∧ ¬H2" is untouched. In every other case the v1 reading stands, including "¬H1 ∧ H3" together with "H2", where another registered interpretation applies and rule 3 therefore does not act. Whenever "¬H1 ∧ H3" applies, E4-H1 is REFUTED and P-PAR is not empty, so E4-H0's registered definition makes it SUPPORTED or REFUTED; rules 1 and 3 cover every reachable case, and any other E4-H0 status is an analyzer inconsistency that fails closed. A D9′ STOP still replaces the reading. The rule-3 outcome is labelled "¬H0 ∧ ¬H1 ∧ H3"; it is a reading outcome, not a new hypothesis or criterion.

note.text: H3 is consistent with opening-pass persistence but is non-discriminating under the global null.

outcome.conclusion: No registered causal interpretation applies; H3 persistence is consistent with, but does not identify, an opening-pass mechanism.

unchanged: E4-H0 to E4-H8 and D9′: statements, supported-if and refuted-if clauses, machine criteria, thresholds and probe priors
